metadata.title: IT Security Operations Overlay SSPP
metadata.remarks: This overlay SSPP constrains the Security Operations SSPP stack for standard enterprise IT environments. It introduces no new authority and does not modify base SecOps roles or workflows.

import-profile.remarks: This overlay constrains—but does not redefine—core SecOps SSPPs.

system-characteristics.system-description: Specializes Security Operations behavior for enterprise IT systems, including endpoints, servers, identities, applications, and cloud platforms.

system-implementation.remarks: IT environments prioritize scale, repeatability, and recoverability. Automation is permitted more broadly than OT or IoMT, but remains bounded by SecOps authority and forensic constraints.

environment-scope.description: User workstations, laptops, and managed endpoint devices.
Virtual and physical servers supporting business applications.
Enterprise identity platforms, directory services, and authentication systems.
IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and cloud-native control planes.

overlay-constraints.statement: SOAR automation MAY be applied more broadly in IT environments but SHALL remain subject to SOAR Authority and Action Boundary SSPPs.
Automated containment actions in IT environments SHOULD be reversible where feasible.
Incident Response in IT environments SHALL account for scale and distributed impact.
Cloud-native monitoring, detection, and response tooling SHALL adhere to same authority and evidence requirements as on-premises systems.

environment-specific-guidance.statement: Endpoint isolation, credential revocation, and process termination MAY be automated when preconditions are met.
Identity actions such as account disablement MAY be automated, but SHALL be logged and attributable.
Cloud resource quarantine and network segmentation MAY be automated if reversible and observable.

control-implementation.description: Controls adapt base SecOps requirements for enterprise IT scale.

implemented-requirements.remarks: IT systems are monitored at scale for security-relevant activity.
Incident handling accounts for distributed enterprise IT environments.
Automation actions are constrained to least-privilege capabilities.

statements.statement: IT scale SHALL NOT justify bypassing escalation, forensic, or evidence requirements.
Cloud or managed service abstractions SHALL NOT introduce implicit authority.
Automation failures in IT environments SHALL escalate as control violations.
Enterprise convenience SHALL NOT override Negative-Pattern Enforcement SSPP constraints.

back-matter.remarks: This overlay is the default SecOps specialization. OT and IoMT overlays SHALL introduce stricter constraints, not looser ones.
